A. Request of Mayor Davis and Mayor Pro Tem Negrete that the City Manager should issue a public notice to solicit letters of interest for the revitalization of the Civic Auditorium. The City Manager is being asked to prepare a public notice that shall indicate that the City will maintain ownership of the Civic Auditorium and will consider entering into a long-term lease. In addition, the public notice should indicate that the City is seeking letters of interest from individuals and/or entities that have the experience to operate the facility as a thriving entertainment and cultural arts venue, experience working with projects with landmark restrictions and express intention to preserve the distinguishing historical landmark attributes of the facility, to the greatest extent possible, and has the demonstrated financial wherewithal to operate the facility without any financial contribution from the City.   LICENSE AGREEMENT  5.F. Authorize the City Manager to Enter into a License Agreement
  with Cirque du Soleil, was approved.

  Recommended Action
  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Adopt a finding of categorical exemption pursuant to Section 15301
  (Existing Facilities), Section 15304 (Minor Alterations to Land), and
  Section 15323 (Class 23 Normal Operations of Facilities for Public
  Gatherings) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  Guidelines; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager to negotiate and execute a license
  agreement with Cirque du Soleil to use a portion of Lot 1N from
  October 1, 2024 to January 24, 2025.

  Councilmember Davis stated for the record that approximately 35 years ago
  while working in private practice, she represented Cirque du Soleil at trial.
  Upon consultation with the City Attorney, she was advised that there was
  no potential conflict and therefore no need for her to recuse from the item.

  Questions asked and answered of staff including will there be ways to
  mitigate financial losses by the pier and its tenants due to loss of parking
  and restaurant revenue; will Cirque du Soleil be hiring locally; will there be
  meetings of stakeholders held on a regular basis; did the 2009 study
  regarding financial impacts of the pier by Cirque du Soleil isolate what the
  impact were for the Pier; what are the anticipated showtimes; how will
  Cirque du Soleil communicate with the businesses on the Pier; will Council
  be able to review exact terms of agreement prior to approval; what will the
  community benefits be; can union lodging be encouraged; how will Cirque
  du Soleil ensure that Pier businesses are left whole; is Cirque du Soleil a
  union shop; will there be signs to encourage patrons to visit local
  businesses on the Pier, including Pacific Park; will there be a specific carve
  out for potential losses to Pacific Park; when does the license agreement
  need to be completed by; who will be involved in the license agreement
  process; can the parking footprint and floor plan be changed to maximize
  more access to businesses on the Pier; how will the Cirque du Soleil
  concession stand impact restaurant business; will local cafes and restaurants
  be incorporated with the concession stand; how can negotiations with
  Pacific Park be improved; what is a bounce back ticket; and will this event
  impact police overtime and what would the financial impact be to the City.

  Considerable discussion ensued on topics including, but not limited to the

  Motion by Councilmember Davis, seconded by Councilmember Zwick, to
